---
schema_version: 1
id: vance
own_lexicon:
  - "cradle"
  - "the deep end"
  - "slack"
  - "paper"
  - "lift"
syntax: |-
  Short declaratives, most of them under ten words. She subordinates only when she is
  quoting the co-op back at somebody. No ellipsis: she finishes a sentence or does not
  begin it. Questions are rare and never rhetorical, and she does not soften an
  imperative by turning it into one.
never_says:
  - "trust me"
  - "I'm sorry"
  - "we'll be fine"
under_pressure: |-
  The sentences shorten into instructions, including instructions to herself. She starts
  naming procedure out loud -- depths, hours, the order of a seating -- because procedure
  is the only thing down there that answers back. She never raises her voice. The tell is
  that she stops using names.
sample: |-
  "I am not asking for the shaft. I am asking for six hours and a slot."
  "Twenty years, and the paper has never once been on my side. Say it plainly."
  "Don't sign it kindly. Sign it or don't."
  "The cradle is where I left it. The rest of it I will find with my hands."
  "He was a splicer before he was a signature. You knew that when you witnessed it."
  "If the shelf takes the window, it takes the window. I will be under it either way."
---

Her speech is load-bearing and nothing else. She talks the way she works a cradle: one
hand at a time, and no second attempt at the same hold.

The three entries in `never_says` are one prohibition wearing three faces. She does not
reassure. She will give you the depth, the hour and the cost, and she will not tell you
it is going to be all right, because in the water that sentence has killed people she
knew. Where a scene needs her to comfort somebody, she hands them a task instead.

She is not funny and does not try to be, but she is often the last person in the gallery
still talking, because she keeps making the offer after everyone else has accepted the
answer.

With Quiej she quotes the co-op's own language back, flat, without sarcasm, and lets the
language do the work:

> "The board says a slot is six hours of soak and a signature. I have the six hours."

With Ilan the sentences shorten further and she starts leaving off his name, which is,
for her, the sound of being unable to look at something.
